name: Fox Corporation

profile.description: Fox Corporation produces and distributes news, sports and entertainment content. Its Cable Network Programming segment includes FOX News, FOX Business, FS1/FS2, FOX Deportes and the Big Ten Network. Its Television segment includes the FOX broadcast network, 29 owned local stations and the free ad-supported streamer Tubi [3]. Fiscal 2026 (ended June 30, 2026) revenue rose 5% to $17.13B. Q4 revenue jumped 28% to $4.21B on World Cup matches, political advertising and Tubi growth, and Tubi reached 110M monthly active users [1][2]. The company is led by Executive Chair and CEO Lachlan Murdoch [4].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Tubi is a significant new revenue stream built since the 2019 spin-off. It reached 110M monthly active users at fiscal year-end 2026 and contributed to Q4 television advertising revenue rising 108% to $1.5B [1][2]. AI Deployment (1/2): Fox's FY2026 annual report says AI adoption 'accelerated across FOX', with customer-facing initiatives in newsroom efficiency and video experiences and new AI tools plus training for staff, but no AI revenue or savings were quantified [4]. Market Share (1/2): Fox is a major player in live U.S. news and sports, but distribution revenue grew only 4% and it lost the Super Bowl to NBC in FY2026; no category share data was found [2]. Pipeline (0/2): No specific next-generation products with dated revenue visibility were identified. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D expense is reported [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Fox describes its purpose around its role as a trusted news source and an 'ownership mentality' that drives a collaborative, entrepreneurial culture. The purpose is clear but not distinctive, and the $787.5M Dominion defamation settlement undercuts the trusted-source claim [4][6]. Community Impact (2/2): The FOX Forward philanthropy program contributed nearly $10M to communities in fiscal 2024, a specific, company-run program with a stated dollar amount [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP insider statistics show net selling over the last four reported quarters: 2 open-market purchases against 20 sales, including 14 sales in Q1 2026 alone [3].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically on 7 growth-sleeve metrics (10 weight units). FOXA's ~0.9% yield is below the 2% Dividend-sleeve threshold. Weighted sum 8.90/10, rounded to 9. D/E is 65.1% (1.0), and ROE of 14.7% is just below the 15% target (0.98 at 2x weight) [3]. Q4 FY2026 revenue grew 28.1% YoY ($4.212B vs $3.287B, World Cup-boosted), scoring 1.0. The 5-year revenue CAGR is 5.8% (FY2021 $12.909B to FY2026 $17.126B), scoring 0.72 at 2x weight [3]. Forward P/E is 10.7x (derived: the $64.51 price divided by FY2027 consensus EPS of $6.01), scoring 1.0. The provider's forward PEG of 0.78 scores 1.0 at 2x weight. The TTM net margin of 9.8% (FY2026 GAAP net income of $1.685B, down from $2.263B) scores 0.49 [3]. Liquidity: ~4.96M shares/day × $64.51 ≈ $320M/day.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9, PROTECTED): Fox's portfolio is concentrated in live sports and live news. These scarce, real-time rights and events, such as the World Cup that drove a 108% jump in Q4 TV ad revenue, cannot be replicated by generative AI [2]. Fox's own risk factors flag AI-generated deepfakes eroding audience trust and AI tools misattributing information to the company, which are real but secondary risks to a news brand [4]. Tubi's ad-supported library is more exposed to AI-generated content abundance. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI is deployed internally and in video experiences, but no AI revenue is disclosed [4].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Fox has made one genuinely long-term bet. It reshaped itself after the 2019 Disney transaction into a focused live news-and-sports company and invested in Tubi before it was profitable, which now has 110M MAUs [1][3]. However, its identity is defined largely by ratings dominance and partisan positioning. Defamation litigation ($787.5M Dominion settlement) suggests a culture that at times optimized for audience share over its trusted-news purpose [6]. Net insider selling and heavy buybacks add to the finite tilt: weighted shares fell from 595M in FY2021 to 424M [3].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Fox articulates a role as a trusted news source with an ownership culture, but the purpose is not framed as a vision of a better future and has been compromised by conspiracy-theory litigation and the Dominion settlement [4][6].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Fox describes a portfolio model with operating CEOs empowered under Lachlan Murdoch and a collaborative, entrepreneurial culture, and it rolled out AI tools with company-sponsored training [4]. No independent employee-sentiment data was found, and high-profile on-air talent exits and lawsuits point to an adequate rather than high-trust environment [6].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Fox's competitive posture centers on ratings and rights wins, such as lamenting the absence of the Super Bowl, which went to NBC in FY2026. Management does not frame rivals as teachers [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Since its 2019 creation, Fox has shifted from linear-only distribution toward free streaming through Tubi, which now drives ad growth alongside sports and politics [1][2]. The core remains linear news and sports carriage, so the shift is meaningful but not a full reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Investing in Tubi through years of losses to build a 110M-MAU streaming platform was a long-term bet against the linear status quo [1]. However, capital allocation has favored large buybacks, with diluted share count down ~28% since FY2021, and FY2026 GAAP net income fell 26% to $1.685B [3].

investment_thesis: Bull case: Fox owns scarce live-news and live-sports franchises that hold value as the rest of linear TV erodes. FY2026 revenue grew 5% to $17.13B, Q4 grew 28% on the World Cup, and Tubi's 110M MAUs give it a scaled streaming ad platform [1][2]. The balance sheet is conservative (D/E 65%, interest coverage 10x), and the stock trades at 10.7x FY2027 consensus EPS of $6.01 with a forward PEG of 0.78 [3]. Consensus sees EPS of $6.64 by FY2029.
thesis_continued: Bear case: FY2026 GAAP net income fell 26% and diluted EPS fell from $4.91 to $3.90, and FY2027 lacks both the World Cup and the Super Bowl comparisons that shape ad revenue [1][2][3]. Cord-cutting pressures the 4% distribution growth, Fox News carries ongoing defamation and reputational litigation risk ($787.5M Dominion precedent), and insiders have been net sellers [3][6]. Fox filed S-4 and 424B3 registration documents in 2026 for a share-issuance transaction that investors should review [4].
key_catalysts: Q1 FY2027 results and the 2026 U.S. midterm political advertising cycle, following higher political ad spend in Q4 FY2026 [2]
Tubi monetization as MAUs scale beyond 110M, narrowing the gap between engagement and ad revenue [1]
Continued buybacks at ~10.7x forward earnings, supported by ~$3.46/share of TTM free cash flow [3]
key_risks: Defamation and reputational litigation at FOX News; the $787.5M Dominion settlement shows the scale of potential liabilities [6]
Accelerating cord-cutting eroding affiliate fees and the 4% distribution revenue growth [2]
Event-driven revenue volatility: the loss of the Super Bowl to NBC and the absence of World Cup and Olympic-type events can swing ad revenue sharply [2]
